content: When a person experiences getting the wind knocked out of them, it refers to a spasm of the diaphragm caused by a sudden and forceful impact to the abdomen. This paralysis makes it difficult to breathe for a short period of time. A similar effect can also occur if a strong blow is delivered to the back. The mechanical force from this stretching induces a spasm in the diaphragm, similar to the muscle spasm known as a charley horse that occurs in the leg. It typically takes a few seconds for the diaphragm to relax and for normal breathing to resume. Martial artists are often trained to exhale forcefully when struck in the stomach. During a diaphragm spasm, the muscles of the larynx may also contract, producing a high-pitched inspiratory sound known as stridor. This sound can be heard for several breathing cycles as normal respiration is restored. A related but much milder form of diaphragm spasm is singultus, commonly referred to as hiccups.
